question.text: Under the SEBI framework for AIF valuation, the Investment Manager must inform investors with reasons if a per-asset-level valuation deviation exceeds specified thresholds. What are the applicable thresholds?

answer.text: More than 15% between consecutive valuations OR more than 25% in a financial year
More than 25% between consecutive valuations OR more than 50% in a financial year
More than 10% between consecutive valuations OR more than 20% in a financial year
More than 20% between consecutive valuations OR more than 33% in a financial year

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Section 14.14, at each asset level, if there is a deviation of more than 20% between two consecutive valuations, OR a deviation of more than 33% in a financial year, the Investment Manager shall inform investors with reasons including changes in accounting practices, assumptions, or methodology. **The Trap:** 10/20 and 15/25 are underpriced traps. 25/50 is overly lax. **Cross-Exam Context:** III-C (Compliance) touches on disclosure thresholds. XIX-C nails the specific 20%/33% numbers, which appear in the annual PPM compliance test. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Build an auto-alert into your valuation-MIS when any single asset hits 15% quarter-on-quarter — gives you a buffer before the 20% regulatory trigger. Documenting the REASON proactively is what auditors look for, not just the notification.
